watchlist.name: Bodal Chemicals
reasons: Chemicals & Petrochemicals is a leading sector
watchlist.pin_note: Ranked 5th of 8 - the purest H-acid exposure in the cluster and the ONLY name with a second, independent lever: it is itself the applicant in a live DGTR anti-dumping investigation into Beta Naphthol from China. Trades at 1.07x book, barely above the value of eight plants in a business where global capacity is the binding constraint. What holds it back: its Dye Intermediates segment actually FELL 4% in Q1 while margin compressed 11.66% -> 9.72%, and it carries ESM Stage I - a 100% margin requirement, so effectively no MTF. Q2 FY27 (around November) is the decisive test: it is the first quarter that contains the H-acid move at all.

watchlist.name: Bhageria Indust.
reasons: Chemicals & Petrochemicals is a leading sector
watchlist.pin_note: Ranked 2nd of 8. Seven consecutive quarters of sequential revenue growth, margin +255bps - and it pre-dates the H-acid squeeze, so the thesis is optionality rather than the whole case. Watching Q2 FY27 (around November) for the eighth quarter with H-acid realisations in the numbers.

watchlist.name: I G Petrochems
reasons: Chemicals & Petrochemicals is a leading sector
watchlist.pin_note: Ranked 4th of 8, just 0.2 behind Foseco - effectively tied for third, and the comparative note says to read it as a co-equal third if the preference runs to cheapness over quality. A Rs 8.2 Cr loss became a Rs 71 Cr profit with the margin swinging 1,778bps, the largest single-year move in the library. ~5.8x annualised earnings, 1.22x book. The risk is that it is a pure spread business with no control over either end. Watching the PAN-orthoxylene spread and the plasticizer plant starting commercial production in September 2026.

watchlist.name: Foseco India
reasons: Chemicals & Petrochemicals is a leading sector
watchlist.pin_note: Ranked 3rd of 8 - and it placed there despite the WORST valuation score in the cohort, carried entirely by the best durability score. Foundry consumables recur with the customer's production rather than their capex, and technical qualification makes switching risky, so its 22.98% margin is structural where the dye names' margins are cyclical. Against that: 47.2x earnings, 4.77x book, only 4.6% below its all-time high, and ZERO exposure to the H-acid thesis that lifted the sector - part of the recent move is flow it did not earn. Watching whether sales growth holds in the mid-teens (the +78% profit was operating leverage in a good quarter, not a run-rate) and whether it holds up once the chemicals rotation fades.

watchlist.name: Guj Inds. Power
watchlist.pin_note: Ranked 1st of 8 in the chemicals-cluster comparative note. Cheapest name there at 6.3x earnings and 0.83x book, with a 48.4% operating margin that is structural (Khavda solar, near-zero marginal cost) rather than cyclical. Watching the Rs 7,000 Cr lignite decision and the Q3 FY27 500 MW commissioning.
